newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Pioneer firms in Viet-Singapore park invest $156m.
newsitem.headline: Pioneer firms in Viet-Singapore park invest $156m.

text.p: Eighteen pioneer investors will invest $156 million to base manufacturing and technical operations in Vietnam at the Vietnam-Singapore Industrial Park, a Singapore consortium heading the development said on Monday.
The industrial park, located in Binh Duong Province, about 17 kilometres north of Ho Chi Minh City, is being developed by a consortium led by Sembawang Industrial.

The companies that received investment licenses from the Vietnamese government include Swiss group Master Builders Technologies (MBT), Japan's Nihon Packerizing, Liwayway Foods from the Philippines, India's Godrej, Malaysia's
Alcamax Packaging and Singapore's ST Automative.
The industrial park aims to attract multinational companies in pharmaceuticals and healthcare, electrical and electronics, building materials, food and precision engineering.
The park is being developed on a 500-hectare site at around $250 million, including an on-site power plant.
The park's chairman Le Thanh Cung said Binh Duong has attracted 121 foreign investments projects with total investment capital of over $1.0 billion.
